_doc: Single place for the per-network limits that gw-media-content checks (scripts/check.py reads this file; no other file may repeat these numbers). Each rule has value, mark, source (URL) and checked (date read). Marks: P = read in the primary source; S = secondary source or search excerpt only; NV = not verified (the check still applies it as a cautious cap, and the skill asks the user to confirm); C = convention of the skill, not a network limit. To refresh: re-read each source, update value/mark/checked, keep the same keys (check.py looks them up by key and fails closed when one of its RULE_KEYS is missing), run `python3 skills/gw-media-content/scripts/test_check.py`, and update docs/research/social-media.md section 5 with the new reading. Keys read by check.py: x.length, x.url_weight, x.wide_symbol_weight, x.thread_posts, x.image_bytes, x.alt_max, reddit.title, reddit.rules_days, reddit.rules_min_chars, extra_channel.image_formats, linkedin.length, linkedin.image_pixels, linkedin.image_formats, linkedin.alt_max, linkedin.document_bytes, linkedin.document_pages, discord.message, discord.image_bytes, discord.alt_max.

length.note: weighted count: Latin = 1, emoji and CJK = 2

wide_symbol_weight.note: weight of an emoji or wide character

thread_posts.note: a thread of 1 to 4 posts; X has no thread limit

image_bytes.note: 5 MB per image; JPG, PNG, GIF, WEBP

alt_max.note: X does not publish the alt text limit; 1000 is a cautious cap

title.source: no source read (reddit.com blocks automatic reading)
title.note: applied as a cautious cap on the title

rules.value: The subreddit rules must be pasted by the user under «### Rules of r/<subreddit>» in sheet.md, with the date read and the self-promotion rule

rules_days.note: «Rules read:» may be at most this many days old and not in the future; subreddits change their rules without notice

rules_min_chars.note: the pasted rules block of each subreddit has at least this many characters (whitespace collapsed); it proves the rules were pasted, not that they were read

image_formats.note: image formats of a channel that is not x, reddit, linkedin or discord (render.mjs writes .webp and .png; a .jpg is accepted as is)

length.note: post text; longer is an article

image_pixels.note: an image must have fewer pixels than this; weight and aspect ratio are not published

image_formats.note: LinkedIn takes JPG, PNG and GIF, not WebP (section 5.3 of docs/research/social-media.md); every channel without this key takes .webp (a convention of the skill)

document_bytes.note: 100 MB; a PDF is the organic carousel

message.note: characters per message; split longer text into blocks separated by a line with ---

self_promotion.value: Set by each server; no verified rule
